rules.title: FEHA source-of-income and criminal-history screening protections
rules.requirement: Landlords cannot refuse to rent or set different terms based on source of income, including Section 8 vouchers, and must comply with rental assistance paperwork. They may not consider arrests without conviction, sealed or expunged records, or juvenile records, may not use blanket bans on people with criminal history, and may deny based on a conviction only if it is directly related to being a good tenant or safety.
rules.quoted_span: No. California law protects tenants from discrimination based on how a tenant will be paying rent (“source of income”).
rules.effective_date_note: The document gives no effective date.
rules.key_value: No source-of-income discrimination; no blanket criminal-history bans

unverifiable_exemptions: owner-occupied home renting to one additional person

rules.exemptions: Owner occupying a home and renting to one additional person may exclude applicants on protected characteristics; senior housing may limit by age.
rules.conflict_note: The page does not cite specific statute sections. Gov. Code § 12955 is the general FEHA housing provision and is inferred.
